title: Effects of Long-Acting Antiretroviral Therapy on Offspring Immunity in Rhesus Macaques
text:
This study aims to improve HIV treatment for pregnant women by testing a new, long-acting medication that
could prevent HIV transmission to their babies while reducing health risks. We will use a rhesus macaque model
to examine how this new treatment affects both the mothers and their offspring, particularly focusing on the
immune system. The goal is to find a safer treatment that helps prevent mother-to-child HIV transmission and
ensures better health outcomes for both mothers and their children.

title: Role of ABL kinases in regulating DNA damage repair and transcription-replication conflicts in SCLC tumors
text:
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive disease with poor survival lacking effective, long-term treatments.
This project will study the role of the ABL protein in promoting SCLC tumor growth, survival, and metastatic
spread. ABL activity can be targeted with small molecule inhibitors that will be used to impair SCLC tumor
progression and metastasis in pre-clinical models, and will result in the development of new treatments that
improve SCLC patient outcomes.

title: Advancing the development of tools to better understand humoral responses to sapovirus following natural infections
text:
Sapovirus (SaV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) in childhood, yet there is little known about
how natural humoral immunity prevents infection to inform vaccine development. Leveraging our team’s ability
to propagate SaV, we will complete the development of neutralization assays and apply these assays to
biobanked samples from a birth cohort (n=444) to answer fundamental questions about natural humoral immunity
to SaV.

title: Functional genetic basis of KCNB1 encephalopathy
text:
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies are particularly severe infant-onset epilepsies that are
difficult to treat and pose a significant lifetime burden for patients, families, and society. KCNB1,
encoding the Kv2.1 voltage-gated potassium channel, has been associated with developmental and
epileptic encephalopathy and over 400 variants have been identified to date. Functional characterization
of KCNB1 variants will provide insights into the mechanistic basis of channel dysfunction and support
the development of targeted treatments to improve the lives of individuals with developmental and
epileptic encephalopathy.

title: Sirtuin -Dependent Regulation of Tuberculosis and HIV Interactions in Macrophages
text:
Tuberculosis is the leading cause of death in mankind due to infections, and more than 8 million new cases
occur each year with 1.2 million deaths per year. Coinfection with HIV-1 has rendered the control of
tuberculosis very difficult, and we have discovered a new method of augmenting host defense so that both M.
tuberculosis which causes tuberculosis and HIV-1 which causes AIDS can be controlled using a new class of
Sirtuin-based drugs. We propose to develop a new intervention using immunotherapy to simultaneously control
HIV-TB coinfections.

title: Integrative deep learning algorithms for understanding protein sequence-structure-function relationships: representation, prediction, and discovery
text:
The growing large-scale data of protein sequences, structures, and functions provide tremendous opportunities
for life science, synthetic biology, precision medicine, and other areas. This project will develop integrative
computational frameworks to advance our understanding of many topics centered around protein biology,
including protein function characterization, structural and functional genomics, disease biology, and protein
design. Successful completion of this project will result in new analytic tools and algorithms for a wide range of
biomedical applications to help improve human health, such as drug discovery, vaccine development, and
personalized diagnosis and treatment.

title: Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium (PC3): A collaborative approach to an enigmatic cancer
text:
Prostate cancer is more common than many other cancers, but its prognosis is highly heterogeneous. This
project builds the foundation for the new Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium (PC3), which brings together 10
prospective cancer epidemiology cohorts to evaluate the potential for precision prevention in men with prostate
cancer based on molecular subtype and to improve at-diagnosis risk stratification tools for prostate cancer
death and cardiovascular disease.

title: Understanding the Development of Mucosal Immunity to Poliovirus: Adjuvants and Modulation of the Enteric Microbiota
text:
Critical to polio eradication efforts is development of new vaccines that stimulate effective mucosal immunity in
the gut to control viral shedding and eliminate environmental reservoirs of poliovirus (PV). This project will provide
critical information to better understand the immunologic and microbiologic factors impacting development of
effective mucosal immunity to PV. It will also assess the effect of a novel mucosal adjuvant (dmLT) on systemic
and mucosal immune responses to Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccines (IPV). The goal of these investigations is to
guide future studies directed at harnessing immune-microbiota interactions to enhance mucosal immune
responses to polio vaccines and other enteric pathogens.

title: Identifying Collaborating Factors Driving DDX41 Mutant Pathology in MDS
text:
Germline mutations in DDX41 are prevalent in adult-onset myelodysplastic syndromes. The proposed research
is relevant to public health because it will delve into how DDX41 insufficiency cooperates with age-associated
inflammation and secondary somatic mutations to affect blood stem and progenitor cells and erythropoiesis. The
findings will have implications for identifying biomarkers and treatments for myelodysplastic syndrome.

title: Molecular basis of MED12 in the pathogenesis of uterine fibroids
text:
Uterine fibroids (UFs; leiomyomas) are the most important benign neoplastic threat to women’s health worldwide.
Current treatment options are limited beyond surgery, and the development of more effective medical therapies
will require a better understanding of the underlying molecular pathogenesis of UFs. Accordingly, this proposal
is impactful as it suggests a novel etiological basis to explain the development of MED12 mutation-positive UFs,
the predominant UF subtype, through aberrant myometrial stem cell differentiation and transcription-dependent
replication stress, and further offers proof-of-concept for therapeutic intervention using drugs that target the
replication stress phenotype. The studies proposed herein thus address and mechanistically connect two
overarching issues in the field: the pathogenesis of UFs and the development of non-hormonal treatment options.

title: eDyNAmiC-TEXASSW
text: eDyNAmiC (extrachromosomal DNA in Cancer) Human genes are arranged on 23 pairs of chromosomes, but in cancer, tumour-promoting genes can free themselves from chromosomes and relocate to circular, extrachromosomal pieces of DNA (ecDNA). These ecDNA do not follow the normal “rules” of chromosomal inheritance, enabling tumours to achieve far higher levels of cancer-causing oncogenes than would otherwise be possible, and licensing cancers with a way to evolve and change their genomes to evade treatments at rates that would be unthinkable for human cells. The altered circular architecture of ecDNAs also changes the way that the cancer-causing genes are regulated and expressed, further contributing to aggressive tumour growth. These unique features make ecDNA-containing cancers especially aggressive and difficult to treat. Cancer patients whose tumours harbour ecDNA have markedly shorter survival. Despite being first seen over fifty years ago, the critical importance of ecDNA has only recently come to light, and the scale of the problem is substantial. ecDNAs are present in nearly half of all human cancer types and potentially up-to a third of all cancer patients. The collective current understanding of how ecDNA form, how they function, how they move around the cell, how they evolve to resist treatment, how they impact the immune system, and how they can be effectively targeted are lacking. We bring together an internationally recognized, pioneering interdisciplinary team of cancer biologists, geneticists, computer scientists, evolutionary biologists, mathematicians, clinicians, and patient advocates to boldly create novel insights and resources and to provide transformative solutions to one of Cancer’s Grand Challenges. A core team of experienced and productive ecDNA investigators will work with new investigators in the ecDNA and cancer fields to bring completely new perspectives and approaches to this daunting challenge. By bridging cutting-edge and diverse approaches and insights from cancer genomics, yeast genetics, epigenomics, artificial genome synthesis, longitudinal patient tracking, combinatorial and machine learning algorithms, mathematical modelling, immunobiology, and innovative chemistry we will develop a new understanding of the role of ecDNA in cancer, and we will find new ways to drug the undruggable. This bold programme, which consists of 7 work packages and a committed international infrastructure, generates new and unusual collaborations that would simply be impossible under any other type of funding mechanism. Our programme endeavours to foster bold innovative solutions to one of the hardest problems in cancer and to one of the greatest challenges facing cancer patients.

title: Subjective and Somatic Tinnitus; Using Functional Near-Infrared-Spectroscopy to Identify Objective Correlates in Auditory and Non-Auditory Cortices
text:
Tinnitus, phantom sound perception, is a common problem that leads to neural changes within primary
auditory cortex. Utilizing an innovative fNIRs probe that we adapted to the ear canal from a previous R21 grant,
we are now capable of localizing brain changes (possible tinnitus corelates; hemodynamic responses and
resting state functional connectivity) in human tinnitus that is both subjective and somatic (modulated by head
and neck maneuvers). Our current proposal will fill a vital need in the field, as we will be able to closely
measure both types of tinnitus in humans as well as corelate those changes with severity levels in those who
can and cannot modulate perception with head and neck movements.

title: Software tools for creating standardized multimodal EHR datasets for advancing ophthalmic research using AI
text:
Ophthalmology relies on multimodal EHR data, but inconsistencies and lack of standardization impede its
effective use for research and clinical care. AI-driven tools leveraging NLP and LLMs can address these
challenges by improving data quality, extracting key clinical concepts, and standardizing datasets. These
advancements will facilitate more accurate disease progression prediction, streamlined clinical workflows, and
effective data harmonization, ultimately advancing clinical research and enhancing patient care.

title: Data Science and Statistics Core
text: Abstract Data Sciences and Statistics Core The Data Sciences and Statistics Core (DSSC) will be a multi-site core that integrates experts in data management, biostatistics, epidemiology and pathogen genomics. First, the DSSC will serve as an inventory hub for all data associated with this program, including sample inventory, epidemiologic data, and microbial genomic sequence data. With complex epidemiologic data and terabytes of genomic sequence data from over 16,000 isolates and nearly 3,000 plate metagenomes, a detailed inventory is essential to ensure organized access. Second, the DSSC will be a data sharing hub across all Projects. The DSSC will be responsible for facilitating secure and frictionless data transfer between Projects, maintaining consistent nomenclature across data types, as well as detailed data dictionaries. This resource will be essential to enable synergistic collaboration between researchers across multiple institutions and projects, working with large, complex datasets. Third, the DSSC will serve as an innovation hub for integrating biostatistics traditionally used for epidemiologic studies with computational biology for genomic analysis. Researchers with expertise in statistical modeling, epidemiology and bioinformatics will work closely to develop novel methodology for the simultaneous analysis of complex epidemiological and genomic data. The DSSC will provide data science and biostatistical expertise across all projects. This will enhance the synergy among the projects by unifying data and statistical consultation. In convening an integrated core with expertise in biostatistics, computational biology, epidemiology, and genomics, we will form a unique and powerful platform for developing novel approaches and provide the clearest view of multidrug resistant organism (MDRO) carriage and transmission within nursing homes (NHs) to date.

title: Decoding the Neural Representations of Movement Minimally Invasively via Functional Ultrasound
text:
Brain machine interfaces (BMIs) offer patients suffering from neurological injury and disorder the ability to
regain their autonomy by providing control of assistive devices using their thoughts. Current BMIs are
constrained by the requirement of invasive surgical implantation and the technical limitations of current
neurorecording techniques, limiting the patient pool able to access BMIs and our understanding of motor
variable encoding at the mesoscopic level. This study aims to use the novel neurotechnology, functional
ultrasound (fUS), coupled with electrophysiology to bridge our understanding of macroscopic and microscopic
motor representation in the primary motor cortex and posterior parietal cortex and expand the accessibility of
BMIs through the development of a more minimally invasive fUS-based motor BMI, demonstrating fUS’
potential for future clinical applications such as chronic neuropsychiatric monitoring and closed-loop
neuromodulation.

title: Core 5 - Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core
text:
This core will help analyze a large, randomized phase III study comparing two consolidation treatment schedules 
for MRD negative patients to determine the role of HDT and role of single versus tandem HDT for MRD positive 
patients to inform therapeutic approaches. The core will provide bioinformatic support to unravel and integrate 
the genomic changes to better understand disease biology, features predictive of progression and define those 
changes able to predict outcome and inform the development of novel therapeutics.

title: Revealing the Role of Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation in Plasmodium falciparum Transcriptional Regulation
text:
All cells need to have mechanisms in place to cope with protein misfolding and aggregation. The proteome of
the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum presents a significant challenge in this regard due to a high
preponderance of poly-Asn repeat regions that is higher than any other known organism. This study will uncover
how P. falciparum maintains protein homeostasis by focusing on asparagine-rich members of the ApiAP2
transcription factor protein family and the activity of the essential chaperone Pf Hsp110c, providing valuable
insights that could lead to the development of novel antimalarial drugs disrupting proteostasis.

title: Informatics-enhanced Social Networks and Affiliation Processes (ISNAP) to promote risk reduction and early diagnosis of Alzheimer's and Related Dementias.
text: Our proposed research seeks to elucidate information-seeking phenomena, specifically for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD). By employing advanced methodologies in data science and social network analysis, the study aims to uncover the inter-personal and intra-personal mechanisms through which we can support ADRD risk-reducing and care-seeking efforts. The ultimate goal is to inform the development of more precise and targeted interventions and campaigns that can enhance health promotion and ADRD detection strategies within at-risk communities.

title: Mechanism and Role of Membrane Fusion by the Atlastin GTPase
text:
Atlastin (ATL) GTPases are required for shaping the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), an essential subcellular
organelle whose structure is important for many cellular processes. Importantly, mutations in the neuronal
ATL1 paralog cause the human motor neurological disorder hereditary spastic paraplegia, but how neuronal
ATL1 or the nonneuronal ATL2/3 paralogs are regulated to maintain ER structure in their respective cell types
remains unknown. The proposed studies seek to uncover how this basic cell biological process is regulated as
well as the basis for the human disease resulting from its dysfunction.

title: Identifying inhibitors of the bacterial peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase
text:
Peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase is an enzyme that is critical for growth of bacteria, including bacterial pathogens.
No inhibitors of the peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase are currently known that can be used for treatment of bacterial
infections. We will implement a novel approach to identify such inhibitors that could be subsequently developed
into the clinically useful antibiotics suitable for curing diseases caused by harmful bacteria.
